request-lifecycle.0: Does not describe how the request reaches the backend.
request-lifecycle.1: Mentions that a POST request is sent but omits routing or middleware.
request-lifecycle.2: Describes the full request path: form submit -> HTTP client -> route -> view/handler.
request-lifecycle.3: Explains the complete lifecycle including Content-Type, body parsing, and which middleware or authentication class runs before the handler.

credential-issuance.0: Does not mention that a credential or token is created.
credential-issuance.1: Knows something is returned to the client but cannot explain what it is or how it is produced.
credential-issuance.2: Explains the call that creates it (jwt.sign / jwt.encode / RefreshToken.for_user) with the payload and the secret or signing key.
credential-issuance.3: Explains the payload, the signing algorithm, the expiry, and where the client stores the result — and can say what is deliberately left out of the payload.

password-verification.0: Does not mention how the submitted password is checked.
password-verification.1: Knows a hash is involved but cannot explain the verification step.
password-verification.2: Explains the comparison the stack actually uses (bcrypt.compare, Django authenticate/check_password, argon2 verify) against the stored hash.
password-verification.3: Explains the comparison, why it is constant-time, which hasher is configured and where its parameters live, and what a mismatch returns.

error-handling.0: Does not mention any error handling.
error-handling.1: Mentions a 4xx status but cannot say what triggers each one.
error-handling.2: Describes at least two failure cases (wrong password, unknown user, expired token) with the right status codes.
error-handling.3: Describes every failure case it handles, uses the right codes, avoids revealing which field was wrong, and says what happens to the request after the error (transaction rollback, audit log, retry).

hints: Start at the form submit and name each hop until the response.
Which call issues the credential, and what is inside it?
How is the submitted password checked against what is stored?
